---
title: "Where wrapping stops"
---

The figure wraps the paragraphs that follow it. Wrapping stops at the first
block that is not a paragraph, and that block starts below the figure.
Examples of blocks that are not paragraphs are a heading, a list, a table,
a code block, a callout, another figure, and a horizontal rule. A wrapped
[table float](get-started.qmd#wrap-a-table) stops at the same blocks in
HTML and PDF through Typst.

::: demo
![Mean ratings by condition.](images/ratings.png){#fig-list .wrap-right width="35%"}

This paragraph wraps beside @fig-list, and so does the next one.

The list after this paragraph is not a paragraph, so wrapping stops there.
If the text beside a figure is shorter than the figure, the space beside
the figure stays empty:

- The list starts below the figure.
- It runs the full width of the column.
:::

An image with no caption and no wrap class counts as a paragraph. Quarto
expands `{{{< include >}}}` before the filter runs, so the included blocks
follow these rules as written.

## Stop wrapping earlier

To stop wrapping earlier, put an empty `wrap-clear` div after the last
paragraph that you want beside the figure:

```markdown
::: {.wrap-clear}
:::
```

::: demo
![Mean ratings by condition.](images/ratings.png){#fig-clear .wrap-left width="35%"}

Only this paragraph sits beside @fig-clear.

::: {.wrap-clear}
:::

An empty `wrap-clear` div comes before this paragraph, so it starts below
the figure.
:::

In PDF through LaTeX, in PDF through Typst, and in Word, wrapping stops as
in HTML, and a `wrap-clear` div works.

## Shortcodes

A paragraph that shows only one shortcode can also stop wrapping, because
the shortcode can make a block. Spaces, line ends in the source, HTML
comments, and one span around the shortcode show nothing, so
`{{{< video URL >}}} <!-- note -->` and `[{{{< video URL >}}}]{.my-class}`
stop wrapping too. Examples are a `{{{< pagebreak >}}}` page break and a
`{{{< video >}}}`, which is a block in HTML and a link line in the other
formats. This holds for a shortcode from another extension too, even one
that makes text.

Eight Quarto shortcodes usually make text, an image, or paragraphs:
`meta`, `var`, `env`, `kbd`, `lipsum`, `placeholder`, `version`, and
`brand`. A paragraph with one of them counts as a paragraph, also with a
comment beside it. The next paragraph gives the one exception.

If a `{{{< meta >}}}` shortcode is all that its paragraph holds and its
value holds a block other than a paragraph, wrapping stops. Examples of
such blocks are a list and a code block. A `meta` value of paragraphs only
counts as paragraphs. With a comment or a span around it, Quarto renders a
`meta` value as text, so the paragraph counts as a paragraph.

## A figure with nothing to wrap

A wrapped figure with no paragraph right after it keeps its normal layout.
An example is a figure right before a heading. Another is a figure right
before a paragraph that stops wrapping under the rules above. An example of
such a paragraph holds only a `{{{< video >}}}` and a comment. In HTML,
LaTeX, Typst, and Word the render prints no warning for such a figure. The
places on [Where a figure keeps its normal layout](normal-layout.qmd) are
the exception: a figure there prints its warning with or without a
paragraph after it.

## Two figures in a row

Of two wrapped figures in a row, the first keeps its normal layout, and the
second wraps the paragraphs after it. This does not hold for the figures of
one code cell, which [Where a figure keeps its normal
layout](normal-layout.qmd#code-cells-with-more-than-one-figure) covers.
